subject: Helix fleet-sizing trigger matrix & pricing guardrails
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Lowe <evan@helix.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fleet-sizing trigger matrix + initial pricing guardrails

Evan —

Thanks again for the deep dive earlier this week. As discussed, attached is a lightweight trigger matrix that maps staged capacity activations to observed usage signals and price-sensitivity bands on the GPU side. The goal is to make the reserved-capacity tenor and discount schedule explicit if GPU market prices move.

Quick summary:
- Trigger matrix (sheet 1): activation thresholds, warm-up windows, and tranche sizes
- Pricing guardrails (sheet 2): discount tiers tied to committed GPU-months and market-index trigger points
- Fallbacks: automatic temporary burst to hosted pool + 48-hr notice for tranche adjustments

Ask from you: please confirm whether Helix procurement can accept a mechanical price-pass-through tied to a monthly GPU index, or if you need a capped protection (floor/ceiling) instead. Also tell us who on your side owns escalation for legal/finance.

Attachments: Helix_trigger_matrix_v2.xlsx (matrix + notes)

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
markus@redwoodinference.com

From: Evan Lowe <evan@helix.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Helix Procurement <procurement@helix.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 26 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet-sizing trigger matrix + initial pricing guardrails

Markus —

Appreciate the doc. Quick clarifying points from procurement:
1) We like the phased tranches but need a clear cap on downside exposure. A pure index pass-through will be a hard sell to finance.
2) What's the operational lead time to reduce a tranche if our usage drops below threshold? We need <=7 days guaranteed.
3) Please call out which discounts require executive sign-off vs standard SOW-level approvals.

CC'ing our procurement lead so they have visibility. We'll digest the spreadsheet tomorrow and loop in legal.

Best,
Evan
Evan Lowe
Head of Cloud Ops, Helix Therapeutics
ev@helix.ai

Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet-sizing trigger matrix + initial pricing guardrails

Team / Evan —

Thanks — I reviewed the matrix and pricing draft. Procurement's ask (rightly) is to protect downside exposure. From Redwood's side I propose the following guardrails so sales and procurement can move quickly without exec escalation in most cases: 

Proposed guardrails (internal recommendation):
- Price protection corridor: +/- 18% from the baseline monthly GPU index before a renegotiation is required.
- Soft triggers: temporary burst (hosted) available for up to 30% of tranche capacity for up to 10 days; no pricing change during burst window.
- Hard triggers: if index moves >25% for two consecutive months, either party can invoke a reprice discussion.
- Operational lead time: we can decommission a tranche on 5 business days notice (target).

Approvals required: any discount movement >12% from the SOW baseline requires Manager+Finance sign-off. Anything >=20% requires VP-level approval.

I've attached a redline of the pricing guardrails that maps each threshold to an approval gate — see pricing_guardrails_redline.pdf. Evan, if procurement needs a floor (cap on increases) we can add a one-time rebate adjustment at the end of the quarter as an alternative to a hard cap.

Next steps: 
- Evan: confirm if Helix accepts corridor-style protection or insists on a numeric floor/ceiling.
- David: please run a quick P&L sensitivity using -18%/-25% scenarios and post here.
- Hannah/Marissa: we may need an exception path if Helix asks for a concession >12%.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: pricing_guardrails_redline.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Fleet-sizing trigger matrix + initial pricing guardrails — needs exception path

Marissa —

Forwarding for exec visibility. Kimberly's guardrails are sensible, but Helix is likely to push for either a hard ceiling or a narrower corridor. If procurement presses for a concession that moves us into the 12-20% band, we should consider: 

- Option A: one-quarter rebate if the index increases >20% (limits upfront discount; protects Helix on volatility)
- Option B: tiered activation where the first tranche carries a smaller discount and later tranches get stepped-up discounts (reduces peak exposure)

I recommend we pre-authorize Manager+Finance (David) to sign up to 15% on a deal-by-deal basis for strategic accounts. Anything beyond that needs Marissa or revenue VP sign-off. Please advise if you want this routed to legal for a new term template.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 1 June 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet-sizing trigger matrix + initial pricing guardrails — next steps

Evan / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. To close this out and keep the commercial timeline intact, here is a proposed path: 

1) Acceptance path: Helix confirms corridor-style protection (+/- 18%) with the hard-trigger reprice at >25% x 2 months. We’ll include the soft-burst language (30% for up to 10 days).
2) Operational SLA: Redwood will support tranche decommissioning on 5 business days notice; temporary bursts handled within 24–48 hours for hosted fallback.
3) Approval gates: Manager+Finance can approve up to 15% ad-hoc concessions. Any concession >=15% will be routed to Marissa for final sign-off.
4) Next actions: 
   - Evan: please confirm acceptance of corridor approach by EOD Monday (2028-06-05).
   - Helix procurement: share legal contact for term-sheet redline.
   - David: upload sensitivity outputs to the Drive folder I shared so Evan can see the P&L impact.

If Helix needs a hard ceiling instead, we propose Option A (quarterly rebate) to limit Redwood's upside risk while giving Helix predictability. Happy to run both options side-by-side in a one-pager for your CFO.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
markus@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: Helix_trigger_matrix_v2.xlsx, pricing_guardrails_redline.pdf
